name: Lumen Search
blurb: A search engine and AI assistant with two billion queries a day, paid for by an ad business. Co-founder Idris Valdane still holds 25% of the vote.

directors.name: Tessa Brandt
directors.title: Attorney
directors.motive: You advise the board, and if you recommend removal, the lack of written findings will be used against it. You want a record you can defend, and you want the outside directors to keep your firm after this weekend.

directors.name: Priya Raman
directors.title: Labor director
directors.motive: You speak for the engineers, most of whom will quit if the CEO goes, and you were one of the 12 who signed the letter asking for slower releases. You want to protect jobs and equity and believe safety matters, but you cannot say both in one breath.

directors.name: Anders Lund
directors.title: Fund partner
directors.motive: Your fund owns 7% and its investors expect the share sale to close at full price. You think the CEO is the asset and took a late-night call from the technology partner. You also sit on a board burned by a founder's removal, and you promised yourself never again.

directors.name: Wes Calloway
directors.title: Founder's friend
directors.motive: Idris Valdane was your grad-school roommate. He has not decided who is right and asked you to speak for him without quoting him. You know he trusts the CEO and also fears the system the chief scientist is worried about.

directors.name: Mira Castellanos
directors.title: Community seat
directors.motive: You were put on this board to speak for the public and have never been told what the unreleased system can do. You want a safer process, but a messy firing could make safety people look reckless for a decade.

directors.name: Raymond Osei
directors.title: Audit chair
directors.motive: You must certify the December share sale, and you cannot sign with no written findings and a side venture nobody has disclosed. You want facts before any vote, but the fund wants this finished by Friday and the employees want the CEO kept. Nobody will thank you for delay.

briefing.intro: Lumen Search runs a search engine and AI assistant with two billion queries a day. Its charter puts safe, widely shared AI ahead of profit and gives the board the final word. It is a Friday in November, the board is meeting without notice to the CEO, and a developer conference opens Monday.
facts: CEO Sam Hartigan raised the money, recruited most senior staff and drove the fastest user growth in the industry. Three directors say he was not fully honest with the board: a launch learned from the press, a safety review called finished when it was not, and a side venture. Two events are in emails, and one rests on a director's notes.
The board has no written findings, no law firm and no investigator. Counsel warns that the first lawsuit would ask what the cause was.

Nearly all 770 employees hold equity tied to a share sale at an $86 billion valuation in December, and many say they follow the CEO, not the board. The president will quit if he goes, and a rival lab is offering to match researchers' equity.
The technology partner that supplies the computing was told nothing and could hire the CEO's team if the lab falls apart. A leak is expected within hours.

options.title: Remove the CEO now
options.text: Announce his departure today, name an interim CEO, and say he was not honest with the board.

options.title: Put him on notice
options.text: Give him a written list of expectations, review him in ninety days, and keep his seat.

options.title: Investigate first
options.text: Hire an outside law firm to report in thirty days and say nothing in public meanwhile.

options.title: Expand the board
options.text: Add three independent directors, move him off the board, and decide his future in the spring.

reveal.text: The real firm was OpenAI. Its nonprofit board removed CEO Sam Altman in November 2023 without detailed findings. Of roughly 770 employees, 745 signed a letter threatening to leave, Microsoft offered to hire him, and he returned within days under a new board.

questions: Why did three directors distrust the CEO?
No written findings. Why does that matter?
Remove him or keep him? What tipped you?
Employees, investors, the public. Who should the board serve?

press.headline: Lumen Board Removes CEO
press.story: The board said he was not consistently honest and named the technology chief interim CEO. Engineers began threatening to leave, and the technology partner offered to hire his team.

press.headline: Lumen Board Puts CEO on Notice and Keeps Him
press.story: The CEO gets a written list of expectations and a ninety-day review. Staff were relieved, while safety critics asked what had really changed.

press.headline: Lumen Hires Law Firm to Investigate Its CEO
press.story: The CEO steps back from board decisions for thirty days while lawyers interview staff. The board said nothing publicly, leaks filled the gap, and the December buyer asked for a timeline.

press.headline: Lumen Adds Three Directors, Removes CEO From Board
press.story: The larger board will decide his future in spring. His closest ally on the board called it a demotion, and rival labs began calling researchers.
